pe.definition: Price-to-Earnings ratio: a stock's price divided by its earnings per share over the last 12 months.
pe.whatItMeans: Shows how many rupees investors are paying for each rupee of profit the company makes. Lower generally means cheaper relative to earnings, but a very low P/E can also mean the market expects trouble ahead.

marketCap.definition: Market capitalization: the total value of all of a company's outstanding shares (share price x number of shares).
marketCap.whatItMeans: A quick measure of company size. StockPilot groups companies into Large/Mid/Small buckets based on this number.

debtToEquity.definition: Debt-to-Equity ratio: a company's total debt divided by its shareholders' equity. Shown as a multiple, so 1.2× means debt is 1.2 times equity.
debtToEquity.whatItMeans: Shows how much a company relies on borrowed money versus its own capital. A lower ratio usually means less financial risk. Banks and other financials show n/a because debt works differently for them, so the ratio isn't comparable.

profitMargin.definition: Net profit divided by revenue, shown as a percentage.
profitMargin.whatItMeans: Shows how much of every rupee of sales a company actually keeps as profit. Higher generally means a more efficient or higher-priced business.

change1m.definition: The percentage change in closing price over the last 4 weeks of available data.
change1m.whatItMeans: A snapshot of recent price momentum. Positive means the stock has risen over that period, negative means it has fallen.
